result.recommendation: Hold Step 5 finalization and assemble a completion-evidence package: attach existing native VS Code scenario traces and the scoped change inventory, then run the explicitly required npm test command. Proceed to user approval only when that package supports the stated acceptance criteria.
result.rationale: The checkpoint reports 11 Linux passes, Windows BLOCKED, an 8.5/10 review, and passing listed commands. Those are favorable reported results, but the supplied excerpts do not connect native VS Code execution to observable delegation and permission enforcement. The shown test checks only that result.cases contains 11 entries; eleven failed or synthetic entries could satisfy that assertion. The runner excerpt contains comments rather than execution evidence, and no trace artifacts are attached. Also, none of the listed validation commands is npm test, despite that being an explicit success criterion. This is an evidence-completeness blocker, not proof that the implementation or reported runs are defective; rerunning already reported passing suites would not resolve it.

Provide a successful npm test result for the candidate being finalized; the listed adapter, qualification, distribution, and release commands do not establish this explicit acceptance criterion.

Provide the actual changed-path inventory and relevant diff evidence establishing zero runtime source modifications, no user-settings edits, and compliance with the authorized scope. Intended changed paths are not evidence of actual changes.

Check the candidate change inventory against authorized_paths and the non-goals; expect no runtime-source or user-settings changes and no unauthorized modified files.
